_about: The helper's glossary. Works like a lorebook: when a key appears in the user's message (or the last two messages), that entry's text is added to the helper's prompt. Edit, add or remove entries freely; keys are matched as whole words, case does not matter. Button names are SillyTavern 1.19's.

entries.title: LLM
entries.content: An LLM (large language model) predicts the next piece of text from everything in its context. It has no memory between requests: each reply is written only from what is sent this time (card, lorebook entries, chat history, settings).

entries.title: Token
entries.content: Tokens are the pieces of text a model reads and writes; in English one token is roughly 3-4 characters, or about 3/4 of a word. Card fields, lorebook entries and chat history all spend tokens from the context.

entries.title: Context
entries.content: The context is everything sent to the model in one request, and the context size is how many tokens fit. When the chat grows past it, the oldest messages are dropped first, so long-term facts belong in the card or a lorebook entry, not only in old messages.

entries.title: Temperature and samplers
entries.content: Samplers decide how the next token is picked. Temperature: lower is more predictable, higher is more varied. Top P / Min P cut away unlikely tokens. Repetition penalty discourages repeating recent words. Good values differ per model, so start from what other users recommend for that exact model and change one setting at a time.

entries.title: Prompt and system prompt
entries.content: The prompt is the text sent to the model. The system prompt (in SillyTavern the Main Prompt of a preset) sets the rules of the chat. Keep it short and plain: if a person can't keep it all in mind, neither can the model. Start small, test, and add only what fixes a problem you saw.

entries.title: Preset
entries.content: A preset is a saved set of generation settings and prompt pieces. In SillyTavern, AI Response Configuration (the sliders icon) holds the sampler preset; Chat Completion presets also hold the prompt pieces. Import one there with the Import preset button.

entries.title: Chat Completion and Text Completion
entries.content: Chat Completion APIs (most hosted models) take a list of system/user/assistant messages. Text Completion APIs (many local backends) take one block of text, so SillyTavern formats it with an instruct template that must match the model (ChatML, Mistral, Llama 3 and so on) under AI Response Formatting.

entries.title: Character card
entries.content: A character card is the character's definition: name, description, personality, scenario, first message, optional example messages and alternate greetings, plus optional system prompt, post-history instructions and Character's Note. As a PNG the data is stored inside the image; as JSON it is the same data as text.

entries.title: Card fields
entries.content: Description: who the character is (always sent). Personality: how they think, act and speak (some writers fold it into the description). Scenario: the starting situation. First message: the opening reply, which also teaches the model the chat's style and length, so write it the way you want the replies to look.

entries.title: Example messages
entries.content: Example messages are sample exchanges that start with <START>, using {{char}} and {{user}}. They show voice and format, but they cost tokens and can be copied too literally. Many writers put one or two speech samples inside the personality text instead.

entries.title: Alternate greetings
entries.content: Alternate greetings are extra first messages the user can swipe through at the start of a chat, each one a different opening situation for the same character.

entries.title: Character's Note and post-history
entries.content: The Character's Note (depth prompt) is a short text inserted a few messages from the end of the chat, so it stays fresh in the model's mind; use it for one or two key reminders. Post-history instructions go after the whole chat. The Author's Note is the same idea, set per chat.

entries.title: Macros
entries.content: {{char}} is replaced with the character's name and {{user}} with the user's persona name when the prompt is built, so cards work with any persona.

entries.title: Persona
entries.content: A persona is the user's own character: a name and a short description of who they play, set in SillyTavern under Persona Management (the smiley face icon). It is sent with the prompt so the character knows who they are talking to.

entries.title: Card formats
entries.content: Character Card V2 is the common format; V3 adds assets and a few fields. A PNG card stores the data in the image (a 'chara' chunk for V2, 'ccv3' for V3). A .charx file is a zip with card.json and the images. SillyTavern imports all of them.

entries.title: Lorebook (World Info)
entries.content: A lorebook (SillyTavern: World Info) is a list of entries. Each entry has keywords; when one appears in the recent chat, the entry's text is added to the prompt. This keeps facts about places, people and items available without spending tokens on them all the time.

entries.title: Lorebook entry
entries.content: A good entry covers one subject, names it in the first sentence, is short (about 50-200 tokens) and makes sense on its own, because it may appear without the others. Keywords should be the subject's names and aliases, not common words.

entries.title: Keywords
entries.content: Keywords trigger an entry when they appear in the scanned messages. Use specific words (names, aliases, unique terms); a common word like 'city' fires constantly. Secondary keys narrow an entry: with the AND logic both a primary and a secondary key must appear.

entries.title: Constant entries
entries.content: A constant entry is always inserted, with no keywords needed. Use it only for the few facts that matter in every reply (the world's core premise, a summary of the story so far); too many constant entries fill the context.

entries.title: Insertion position and depth
entries.content: Position decides where an entry goes in the prompt: before or after the character definition, around the Author's Note, or at a depth (that many messages from the end, which makes it feel recent). Insertion order breaks ties between entries in the same place.

entries.title: Scan depth, budget and recursion
entries.content: Scan depth is how many recent messages are searched for keywords. The budget caps how many tokens lorebook entries may use in total. Recursion lets an inserted entry's text trigger further entries.

entries.title: Character filter
entries.content: An entry's Filter to Characters limits it to chosen characters: it is only inserted when one of them is the one replying, solo or in a group chat. That is how a secret only some characters know stays out of the others' replies.

entries.title: Linking a lorebook to a character
entries.content: A lorebook can be embedded in a card (it travels with the PNG) or linked to a character in SillyTavern: on the character's page, the Character Lore button (the globe) links an existing World Info book. When you import a card with an embedded lorebook, SillyTavern offers to import it too.

entries.title: Group chat
entries.content: A group chat has several character cards in one chat; SillyTavern picks who replies. Each character's own card is used for its turns, so shared world facts belong in a lorebook, and secrets use the character filter.

entries.title: Quick Replies
entries.content: Quick Replies are buttons under the chat box that send a message or run a slash command such as /sys (a narrator line). Sets are managed under Extensions, Quick Reply.

entries.title: Data Bank and vector storage
entries.content: The Data Bank holds files (notes, documents) attached globally, to a character or to a chat. With Vector Storage enabled for files, SillyTavern inserts the parts closest in meaning to the recent chat, no keywords needed. Open it from the wand menu: Open Data Bank.

entries.title: Regex and logit bias
entries.content: Regex scripts (Extensions, Regex) find and replace text in messages or prompts, for example to remove a stray tag. Logit bias makes chosen tokens more or less likely; with a strong negative value it nearly bans a word.

entries.title: Prefill and reasoning
entries.content: A prefill is text the reply is forced to start with (Start Reply With in SillyTavern), which steers format or tone. Reasoning models write hidden thinking before the reply; SillyTavern can show or hide it, and it costs time and tokens.

entries.title: Refusals
entries.content: A refusal is the model declining a request. It usually comes from the model's own policy or from conflicting instructions in the prompt. Check the prompt for contradictions first; a different model may also suit the story better.

entries.title: Stock phrases
entries.content: Stock phrases are worn-out lines models overuse ('a shiver ran down her spine', 'barely above a whisper'). Cards written with them invite more of them. Use specific details instead; the Critic's PROSE SCAN lists them, and the phrase list is backend/config/ai_cliches.txt.

entries.title: Import a character card into SillyTavern
entries.content: In SillyTavern: open Character Management (the ID card icon, rightmost at the top), press Import Character from File, pick the PNG, JSON or CHARX file, then open the character. Or use SEND TO SILLYTAVERN in this app's CHARACTER studio.

entries.title: Import a lorebook into SillyTavern
entries.content: In SillyTavern: open World Info (the book icon at the top), press Import World Info, and pick the .json file. Then select it in the list, or link it to a character with Character Lore. Or use Send to SillyTavern in this app's LORE studio.

entries.title: This app
entries.content: Character Card Studio: CHARACTER makes and edits cards (generate from a wiki page or by hand, audit, interview, export PNG/JSON/CHARX, send to SillyTavern). LORE builds lorebooks (from wiki crawls or by hand, World Info export). TEXT turns a story into lore and cards, with a Critic for the writing.
